status_definitions.PARTIAL: Some capability exists, but the complete requirement is not proven.
status_definitions.NOT BUILT: The proposed platform capability is not present on the public product.
status_definitions.NOT VERIFIED: No sufficient evidence was available; requires execution or access.

findings.finding: The public QEV surfaces do not provide the proposed customer-controlled gateway, connector runtime, SDK onboarding, no-code flow setup, or automatic cross-system evidence capture.
findings.impact: AH Crap Cleanup or an outside company cannot yet test the commercial connector product without custom development.
findings.required_fix: Build one vertical slice: installable gateway, generic signed webhook or OTLP input, event normalization, evidence bundle, storage, verifier, setup wizard, and shadow mode.

findings.finding: The public story presents QEV as a policy-aware workflow platform, a local encrypted vault, a paired-device encrypted chat product, and Proof Lock Labs infrastructure without one clear hierarchy.
findings.impact: A buyer cannot quickly tell what exists today, what the commercial product will become, and which surface is primary.
findings.required_fix: Publish one product hierarchy: Envelope Core, Gateway, Connectors, Flow Packs, Verify, optional Control Plane. Mark each capability Available, Preview, Planned, or Independently Assessed.

findings.finding: The macOS and Windows downloads are not platform-signed. Users are instructed to clear macOS quarantine or click Windows Run anyway.
findings.impact: This is unacceptable friction and a serious trust barrier for a security product and enterprise pilot.
findings.required_fix: Apple Developer signing and notarization, Windows Authenticode signing, signed update metadata, release provenance, SBOM, and downloadable checksum/signature bundle.

findings.finding: QEV publicly states that no formal third-party security audit has been conducted.
findings.impact: QEV cannot honestly issue a broad QEV Protected or Independently Assessed badge.
findings.required_fix: Complete independent cryptographic design review, application penetration test, connector/runtime review, remediation verification, and publish a scoped summary.

findings.finding: The public platform has no KMS/HSM integration, automated key rotation, or revocation.
findings.impact: Commercial users cannot centrally control, rotate, suspend, recover, or audit package access.
findings.required_fix: Implement multi-slot envelope keys, KMS and recipient slots, rewrap, key-version tracking, recovery trustees, revocation boundaries, and key-use audit.

findings.finding: The current Vault V2 flow is a small, one-item envelope rather than a multi-event, large-artifact commercial evidence bundle.
findings.impact: It cannot directly support job photos, legal document histories, long AI traces, or multi-system workflow evidence.
findings.required_fix: Add QEV Evidence Bundle V1 with events, artifacts, streaming encryption, signatures, key slots, gaps, retention, and independent verification.

findings.finding: The crawlable Site Integrity page displays 'Could not load the integrity record. The file may not have been generated yet.'
findings.impact: A trust page that visibly exposes a failure state undermines the core claim. JavaScript execution may change the browser result, so this must be tested manually in multiple browsers.
findings.required_fix: Server-render the current signed record or make the failure actionable; add CI that blocks deployment if the integrity record, public key, manifest, or listed hashes cannot be fetched and verified.

findings.finding: The public repository shows no GitHub Releases while the product site distributes binaries directly.
findings.impact: Reviewers lack a conventional, versioned, signed release record tying source, build, binary, checksums, and notes together.
findings.required_fix: Publish versioned releases with signed artifacts, provenance, checksums, SBOM, changelog, and reproducible or attestable build information.

findings.finding: Public pages report inconsistent test counts: 258 on the main/security pages, 362 on the download page, and 26 tests in the CLI development section.
findings.impact: Reviewers cannot determine what was tested, against which version, on which platform.
findings.required_fix: Publish one generated test matrix broken down by component, commit, version, operating system, and last run. Never hand-edit counts.

findings.finding: The repository root/download page uses @bryan237l/qev-cli while the qev-cli README uses @imagineqira/qev-cli.
findings.impact: Developers may install the wrong or unavailable package and lose trust in maintenance.
findings.required_fix: Choose one official package name, deprecate the other with a clear migration path, and generate every public install command from one source.

findings.finding: The site and apps are described as v0.29.0 while CLI examples and decrypted Vault V2 metadata show v0.28.1.
findings.impact: Cross-version compatibility may be legitimate, but the user is not shown a compatibility explanation or migration status.
findings.required_fix: Publish a compatibility table and display producer version separately from current reader version.

findings.finding: The basic lock flow exposes eight numbered sections, including an auto-picked secret number, scramble code, recipe, and box style.
findings.impact: The interface contradicts the 'zero learning curve' promise and makes standard cryptography look custom or harder than it is.
findings.required_fix: Basic mode should have content, access method, strength recommendation, and Lock. Move non-actionable metadata into an Advanced details panel after creation.

findings.finding: The meaning and security role of 'secret number' and 'scramble code' are unclear in the ordinary user flow.
findings.impact: Users may think they must save additional secrets, misunderstand the threat model, or suspect custom cryptography.
findings.required_fix: Remove these fields from basic mode unless they are required. If retained, rename them with precise cryptographic meaning and make them non-editable technical metadata.

findings.finding: A structured agent receipt decrypts into raw JSON rather than an understandable receipt view.
findings.impact: Business users cannot quickly understand what occurred, what is verified, what is merely claimed, or what is missing.
findings.required_fix: Render known schemas into human-readable timeline, source, artifact, decision, and trust panels, with raw JSON as an advanced view.

findings.status: FAIL BY DESIGN FOR CURRENT VAULT / BLOCKER FOR COMMERCIAL PRODUCT
findings.finding: The current vault states there is no reset, recovery, or recovery key slot.
findings.impact: This is acceptable for a deliberately irreversible one-off vault but not sufficient for company evidence retention.
findings.required_fix: Keep irreversible personal mode, but add organization KMS, recipient key, device, and recovery-trustee slots for commercial packages.

findings.finding: The download page says 'No servers' while also describing encrypted chat with relay delivery.
findings.impact: The wording can be interpreted as contradictory even if the relay cannot read message content.
findings.required_fix: State exactly which operations are offline and which use a relay. Use 'no plaintext server' only where technically true.

findings.finding: The download page says 'The app itself is safe' despite unsigned installers and no formal third-party audit.
findings.impact: An absolute safety claim is not supportable and weakens the otherwise honest threat model.
findings.required_fix: Replace with bounded claims: source available, internal tests passed, artifact hash provided, not independently audited.

findings.finding: Current bundle verification uses HMAC terminology described as a signature, while public site integrity uses Ed25519.
findings.impact: HMAC can authenticate to parties sharing the secret but does not provide public attribution. Buyers may misunderstand what 'signed' proves.
findings.required_fix: Call current HMAC output authenticated unless a precise shared-key signature definition is shown. Use Ed25519 or customer KMS signing for independently verifiable commercial packages.

findings.finding: There is no implemented durable queue, idempotency, duplicate suppression, replay protection, out-of-order handling, backfill, dead-letter queue, or connector self-healing.
findings.impact: Automatic evidence capture would silently lose or duplicate evidence under ordinary provider behavior.
findings.required_fix: Make these P0 gateway requirements and test them through failure injection before live jobs.

findings.finding: There is no implemented company SSO, role mapping, passkey approval, approval-to-artifact binding, or commit-time authorization recheck.
findings.impact: A name in a payload cannot establish who approved the action.
findings.required_fix: Add OIDC/SSO, stable subject IDs, WebAuthn or source-signed approvals, exact action/artifact hash binding, expiry, and authorization revalidation.

findings.finding: There is no implemented shadow mode that records and compares without controlling business operations.
findings.impact: Testing could interfere with AH Crap Cleanup or a customer before capture reliability is known.
findings.required_fix: Add synthetic, historical, shadow, limited-live, automation, then gate-mode stages.

findings.finding: No WCAG 2.2 AA audit, screen-reader test, keyboard test, zoom test, or mobile assistive-technology evidence is published.
findings.impact: A security workflow may be unusable to customers or reviewers with disabilities.
findings.required_fix: Run automated and human WCAG 2.2 AA testing on public pages, gateway admin, customer portal, verifier, desktop, and mobile apps.

findings.finding: The current connector simulator loads without initial JavaScript errors in a local render, has no duplicate static IDs, no horizontal overflow at 1440px or 390px, and has named buttons and external-link protection.
findings.impact: The explainer is structurally usable, but this does not validate the future gateway.
findings.required_fix: Keep it as an explainer; do not use simulator results as evidence that production connectors work.

findings.finding: At the seal stage, the Continue control remains visible but does not advance before sealing and did not show a clear message during the local interaction test.
findings.impact: Users can click a control that appears available and receive no useful response.
findings.required_fix: Disable Continue until sealing succeeds or replace it with one primary Freeze and continue action plus an inline explanation.

findings.finding: Visible checkboxes measured about 15 by 15 CSS pixels in the local mobile and desktop render.
findings.impact: The hit target may be difficult on touch or for users with motor impairments unless the entire label/card is clickable.
findings.required_fix: Ensure the effective hit area is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels and preferably 44 by 44 for primary mobile controls; test label activation.

findings.finding: The CLI describes a generated four-word phrase as roughly 37 bits of entropy.
findings.impact: For a stolen vault subject to offline guessing, that may be inadequate for higher-value or long-retained evidence.
findings.required_fix: Offer risk-based generated phrases, default to substantially stronger random secrets for commercial records, support password managers, and show an offline-attack warning rather than a generic strength label.

findings.finding: The audit could not publicly verify working robots files, complete sitemaps, Search Console coverage, IndexNow keys/submission logs, or canonical rules across all QEV hostnames.
findings.impact: Search discoverability and duplicate handling cannot be called maximized.
findings.required_fix: Add deployment-time SEO validation, sitemap generation, canonical tests, IndexNow logging, and Search Console/Bing reporting.

findings.finding: Public support is primarily an email contact; there is no published status page, incident process, support bundle, support SLA, or recovery runbook.
findings.impact: A customer has no operational path when connectors, packages, keys, or updates fail.
findings.required_fix: Create status, incident, support-bundle, escalation, recovery, and customer-communication processes before external pilots.

test_cases.test: First-time visitor identifies QEV's current product in 10 seconds
test_cases.expected: Visitor states that the current core is a local encrypted evidence envelope and that connectors are the next platform layer.

test_cases.test: Available versus planned capabilities are labeled
test_cases.expected: Every major capability has Available, Preview, Planned, or Independently Assessed status.

test_cases.test: One primary product name is used
test_cases.expected: QEV is primary; BRY-NFET-SX is a protocol/format name; Qira is company; no unexplained Proof Lock Labs identity.
Business user sees Pilot/Flow, developer sees SDK, reviewer sees Verify, ordinary vault user sees Lock/Open.
No unhackable, safe, no-server, audited, court-proof, or complete-reasoning claim exceeds implemented scope.
All pages show the same componentized result for the same release commit.
A nontechnical user locks content with no advanced cryptographic choices and receives a clear save/share instruction.
User selects a vault, enters secret, sees content or a precise error, and can safely clear the screen.
No plaintext appears; generic authentication failure; retry guidance does not leak details.
Decryption fails clearly and is distinguished from wrong file format only when safe.
User sees supported versions, migration options, and no data is modified.
Input limit is shown before work begins and no browser freeze or silent truncation occurs.
Personal mode explains irrecoverability before lock; organization mode offers approved recovery slots.
Generated secret meets configured offline-risk policy and can be copied or saved safely.
Paste/autofill works; no forced composition; long secrets accepted.
Non-actionable values are hidden from basic flow and explained accurately in advanced view.
Known receipt schemas render as a human-readable record with raw JSON optional.
User can clear plaintext, file, phrase, clipboard guidance, and recent state.
After load, all lock/open operations work without network; failure is explicit if dependencies are missing.
Modified script fails closed and the user receives an understandable integrity error.
Vaults from supported web, CLI, desktop, and mobile versions open through golden vectors.
Signed and notarized app opens without quarantine-clearing instructions.
Authenticode-signed installer opens without SmartScreen bypass.
Signed package or container with documented supported distributions.
Signed update checks compatibility, backs up state, migrates, health-checks, and rolls back on failure.
User chooses whether to retain encrypted packages, keys, config, and audit history.
Storage, keys, time, ports, backup, signing, and verifier test pass before activation.
At least two approved recovery paths are tested before production activation.
Non-sensitive support telemetry is off or explicitly approved and previewable.
User sees exact read/write scopes, account, tenant, storage path, and plaintext boundary.
Credential never appears in logs or after save; rotation and revoke tested.
Provider signature is verified over raw bytes and replay protection is enforced.
One non-destructive read proves access and displays data coverage.
User sees history limit, object count, time, storage, and unrecoverable gaps.
Refresh occurs automatically and failure creates an actionable alert.
Connector suspends, records the evidence gap, and does not silently continue.
Exactly one logical evidence event is accepted.
Causal order and late-event handling remain explicit.
Fast durable acknowledgement prevents provider retry storms.
Backoff honors provider limits without losing cursor state.
Every page is processed once and backfill resumes after restart.
Unknown fields are quarantined; required-field loss triggers failure, not silent mapping.
Old and new outputs are compared before authority changes.
Previous version restores without corrupting cursors or duplicating events.
Health status, last-success time, missing period, and recovery are visible.
Operator can inspect, correct, and replay without changing original receipt.
A connection or event ID from another tenant cannot be read or used.
Unused scopes are detected and removal is recommended.
Effect on future capture, retained evidence, and credential deletion is explicit.
Event routes to one case using stable explicit identifier.
Rule and confidence are visible and auditable.
Event enters review queue and is not silently assigned.
No package completion until conflict is resolved or documented.
Event is retained in a queue with expiry and owner.
Rule is previewed against historical examples before activation.
Running case retains starting flow version unless explicitly migrated.
Impact preview, backup, rollback, and package manifest record migration.
Restart or outage does not lose waiting state.
Owner, reminder, fallback, and fail-open/fail-closed behavior are explicit.
QEV observes without changing business action.
QEV compares intended policy without enforcement.
Block occurs only after commit-time identity, artifact, policy, and environment recheck.
Each item is automatic, manual, attested, reference-only, excluded, stale, missing, conflicting, or rejected.
Required, optional, stale, conflicting, excluded, and missing evidence are shown separately.
Package cannot claim complete; flow warns or blocks according to policy.
Reason, approver, expiry, impact, and exact missing item are recorded.
Representative values show full, redacted, tokenized, hash-only, reference, metadata-only, or dropped.
Likely secrets trigger a recommendation and never silently enter logs.
Affected flows/cases and future-only versus retroactive behavior are shown.
Authorized export includes scope and does not expose other tenants or cases.
Deletion respects legal hold, retention, package immutability, and cryptographic-erasure policy.
No plaintext, credentials, package keys, prompts, legal docs, or photos are included.
Hash is captured with source, version, size, media type, and retrieval time.
Multi-gigabyte artifact encrypts without loading fully into memory.
No package is presented as sealed; resumable or clean rollback behavior.
Approval is invalid for new hash and requires reapproval.
Deduplicated while preserving both provenance paths.
Package records failed retrieval and does not claim content possession.
Seal occurs only when completion, evidence, approvals, storage, and signing checks pass.
Creates supplemental or superseding package; original remains unchanged.
Independent verifier validates organization or KMS signature without shared signing secret.
Passphrase, recipient, KMS, device, recovery, and temporary reviewer paths are independent.
Add/remove recipient without re-encrypting all content.
No content exposure and error reveals no sensitive package metadata.
Restored package and manifest verify on a different machine.
Supported old formats remain readable and unsupported formats fail safely.
Timeline, actors, artifacts, sources, gaps, policies, and trust levels are understandable.
Stable subject ID and provider are stored; display name alone is not identity.
Groups map to least-privilege roles and changes take effect predictably.
Approval signs or attests exact action/artifact hash and policy version.
Expired approval cannot authorize action.
Commit-time recheck blocks or re-routes approval.
Flow behavior is explicit; no fallback to weaker local key without approval.
New packages use new version and existing packages remain readable.
Existing content key can be rewrapped with audit evidence.
Affected packages/slots are identified and future access is stopped where controllable.
Two-person or approved recovery is logged and reviewed.
Future controlled access ends automatically; prior plaintext limits are disclosed.
Inactive, external, orphaned, and overprivileged identities are listed.
One QEV job ID creates portal link, folder, calendar reference, and draft package.
Customer identity, exact estimate hash, decision, time, and source are bound.
Offline mobile upload resumes, labels job and before/after state, and preserves file hash.
User can correct assignment without losing original routing history.
Exact changed scope and price require a new approval before work continues if policy requires.
Package shows missing evidence and authorized exception path.
Only required status/amount/reference fields are captured; payment secrets are excluded.
Customer-safe acknowledgement is bound to exact completion summary.
Internal notes and costs never leak into customer package.
Normal operations remain source of truth and QEV cannot block work.
One endpoint change produces a trace preview and no plaintext leaves configured boundary.
One package and initialization records supported model/tool events.
Equivalent behavior and schema to JavaScript.
Request/response forwarding preserves behavior and clearly states observable coverage.
Trace, group, parent, model, tool, guardrail, handoff, and completion IDs are preserved.
User previews metadata, hash-only, redacted, encrypted-full, and excluded results.
UI states that chain-of-thought/provider-internal reasoning is not captured.
Exact tool, arguments, target, user, and policy are approved before side effect.
Requested and returned model/deployment IDs are stored separately.
Source IDs, versions, hashes, and passages are stored only when framework exposes them.
Bounded queue retries without silent drops and reports receipt status.
One completed run automatically creates a package or attaches to configured case.
All actions, dialogs, errors, and data tables are operable without a pointer.
Labels, states, progress, errors, tables, and trust verdicts are announced correctly.
No loss of content or operation and no two-dimensional scrolling for ordinary content.
Effective target size meets WCAG 2.2 and practical field use.
Pass/fail/warning never rely only on color.
Error explains what happened, impact, what was preserved, and next action.
Hosted component outage and impact are communicated.
Customer previews safe diagnostics before sending.
Customer keeps ability to open and verify owned packages using its keys.
Critical control failure immediately changes public certificate status.
Buyer can state exactly what the badge does and does not cover.
Every public host has intended crawl rules and canonical sitemap URLs.
Changed URLs submit with logged 200/202; failures alert; no indexing guarantee is claimed.
Main domain owns commercial content and duplicate GitHub Pages URLs do not compete.
Organization, SoftwareApplication, TechArticle, and breadcrumbs match visible content.
